notesStmt.note: Whitman included this poem in at least two different proof sheets for a cluster of poems that he attempted to publish in late 1890. This manuscript therefore likely dates from some time in 1890 but before December 17, 1890, when Whitman submitted the poem, along with three others, to Scribner's magazine, where it was rejected for publication.
A draft of the poem "Grand is the seen," which was first published in Good-Bye My Fancy in 1891.

lg.head: Grand is the seen
lg.l:
Grand is the seen, the light to me——grand are the
sky and stars,
Grand is the earth and grand are ‸lasting time and space,
And grand their laws so multiform, so puzzling, evolutionary;

Then grander far one's my O unseen soul ‸of mineme; compre-
hending,comprehending,
endowing those,

Lighting the light, the sky and stars, delving the earth,
sailing the sea,
More evolutionary vast, and lasting puzzling, O Soul!
More evolutionary, multiform far, more lasting thou than they
